notes: The conditional implication M001 ⇒ N001 is mathematically valid along S001–S003. All exported clauses are proved using the supplied definitions and the routine facts recorded below. This is local mathematical review; global source identity and controller execution attestation are separate.

applicability.notes: M001 is instantiated with W=X, exponent a and set A. A metric space supplies the induced emetric structure, and X is explicitly equipped with its Borel measurable structure. M001 has no measurability or boundedness condition on A and no exponent restriction; the additional a>0 is retained for the content interpretation. D003 is used only after finite diameter establishes boundedness. There are no E applications.

argument.notes: S001 identifies admissible finite-scale covers and costs, preserves countable costs under empty padding, proves the infimum inequalities and scale monotonicity, and removes r=∞ by domination by any finite positive scale. Every other positive extended scale has a positive real representative, giving exactly the stated supremum. S002 uses the lower-bound property to obtain actual admissible covers and the upper-bound property to force content zero, treating ∞ and an empty admissible class correctly. S003 combines the supremum identity and F002 in both directions. No limit exchange or regularity hypothesis is needed.

dependency_closure.notes: The only direct premise used is M001. F001 is proved in S001 before its use in S002–S003; F002 is proved in S002 before its use in S003. Both retain L1. L2–L6 are discharged within their stated arguments, and L1 is discharged into a>0 at the end. Reindexed families depend only on the chosen countable cover; the small-cover witnesses depend on δ and ε as exported. All other factual uses are routine local facts justified in background_notes; no producer body, ambient H or future fact is needed.

statement_closure.notes: N001 quantifies X,A,a with a>0 and all positive scales/tolerances; its binder explicitly uses X's Borel structure. D002–D006 specify the diameter convention, cost, admissibility, extended codomain and Hausdorff normalization. The real-diameter notation is guarded by boundedness, established for each finite-scale member. Empty costs, countable reindexing, both infimum bounds, monotonicity and both zero criteria are exported explicitly, with no private local witness or unresolved identification.

background_notes.fact: In a metric space, if ediam(B)≤ofReal δ for a finite real δ>0, then B is bounded, diam(B) is finite and nonnegative, and ediam(B)=ofReal(diam(B)). Conversely a bounded B with diam(B)≤δ satisfies this extended diameter bound. Empty B has both diameters zero.

grounds.reason: The finite-scale interpretation is under L2: δ>0, and each member satisfies the displayed extended diameter bound.
ediam is the supremum of pairwise extended distances.
diam is the real supremum for bounded sets, with empty value zero.

background_notes.justification: Each pairwise real distance is at most δ because its extended cast is bounded by ediam(B). For a nonempty B, fixing one point therefore puts B in a ball of radius δ+1; the empty case is bounded as well. The pairwise distance set is nonnegative and bounded above by δ, so taking its real supremum and then casting agrees with its extended supremum. Conversely the supremum bounds all pairwise distances and casts preserve the finite bound.

background_notes.fact: For finite t≥0 and real a>0, the extended power (ofReal t)^a equals ofReal(t^a), and 0^a=0. A supremum of a constant extended cost over proofs of nonemptiness is that cost when the set is nonempty and zero otherwise. Thus at a finite positive scale the D004 summands equal the original nonnegative real diameter powers cast to the extended codomain, including empty members.

grounds.reason: L1 is a>0; under L2 each covering member has finite nonnegative diameter as established there.
D004 specifies the power and supremum over nonemptiness proofs.

background_notes.justification: For t>0 both real and finite extended real powers are exp(a log t); their values agree under the cast. For t=0, the positive exponent gives zero in both conventions. The proof-indexed supremum has either no entries, hence bottom zero, or only repetitions of the same entry.

background_notes.fact: A family of nonnegative extended costs indexed by a countable set I can be transferred along an injection j:I→ℕ with zero outside j(I), preserving its total sum. Applying this to covers with empty padding preserves their union, diameter bounds at positive scales and cost. Finite families are included.

grounds.reason: The proof chooses an injection for a countable index type and puts the unique original member at each image index, with empty sets elsewhere.
D004 uses nonnegative extended sums and gives empty members zero cost.
The original family is admissible at a positive finite scale.

background_notes.justification: Countability gives the injection, including for the empty index type. Injectivity makes the assigned image member unique, so the union is unchanged; the other members are empty and have diameter zero. A nonnegative extended sum is the supremum of finite subsums. Every finite subsum of the original family appears at its finite image, while every finite subsum of the padded family reduces to one on the finite preimage of its intersection with j(I). The two suprema coincide.

background_notes.fact: For any class K of costs in [0,∞], c=inf K satisfies c≤k for each k∈K and b≤c whenever b≤k for every k∈K, with inf ∅=∞. Moreover c=0 iff for every finite real ε>0 some k∈K has k<ofReal ε. Every positive element of [0,∞] has a strictly smaller positive finite real representative. Nested infima with failed conditions valued ∞ equal the infimum over admissible costs.

grounds.reason: D004 takes all costs and infima in ℝ≥0∞ and assigns ∞ to a failed condition.
F001 establishes the infimum bounds used in S002.
S002 fixes positive finite ε and considers the class of admissible δ-covers.

background_notes.justification: The inequalities are the defining greatest-lower-bound properties. Flattening nested infima collects admissible entries; inadmissible entries contribute only ∞, which cannot lower an infimum. If c=0 but there is no cost below ε, ε is a positive lower bound, a contradiction. Conversely a positive finite c admits ε=c/2>0, and c=∞ admits ε=1; a cost below this ε contradicts c≤k. This proves the criterion also when K is empty. These are order arguments, not an attainment assumption.
